_note: Technique registry (issue 0030): the enumerable creative palette the brainstorm samples from, so the host can propose the full producible move-set — not just the thin menu baked into its prompt. Consolidated from docs/glossary.md, references/COMPOSED-CARDS.md (§3 motion, §4 templates), and anatomy-of-a-launch-video.md. Each technique names its backing capability (engine/capabilities/*.json) and a feasibility tag. FIRST-PASS curation: the technique set and especially the combinesWith / clashesWith affinities are a starting point seeded from the documented prose — they are meant to be reviewed and tuned by the craft owner, not treated as final taste.

feasibilityLegend.now: producible today with baked tools (chromium/HyperFrames, playwright capture, ffmpeg, local TTS/music)
feasibilityLegend.now-keyed: producible now but needs an API key in .engine_env (e.g. image generation)
feasibilityLegend.needs-user-footage: producible only when the caller supplies the source footage (edit-footage)
feasibilityLegend.roadmap:video-gen: needs a generative-video service key (not wired)
feasibilityLegend.roadmap:heygen: needs a hosted avatar provider (paid tier, not provisioned)

rule: Every memorable video commits to ONE signature move (CRAFT-BAR §A1); techniques combine, but do not stack 4+ signature-grade devices (that is the AI-slop cluster). Pick a signature, support it with compatible techniques, keep the §A3 tell count 0-1.

techniques.name: Kinetic typography / payoff card
techniques.description: Heavy-weight type on a flat saturated ground, one sentence or phrase, tight tracking — the hook or the close as a single-idea card (COMPOSED-CARDS §4).
examples: Single-idea title/payoff card
a declarative one-line close

techniques.name: Morphing element (label/icon swap)
techniques.description: A chip/pill that cycles real options inside your own sentence, or a symbol that swaps state — one plate per state, cut on the beat. Shows range or change without a list (COMPOSED-CARDS §3/§4 'morphing-pill breadth hook').
examples: a pill cycling supported platforms inside one sentence
a status pill flipping draft->published

techniques.name: Colour-per-beat section grounds
techniques.description: Each beat gets its own flat saturated ground colour; the change of colour between beats IS the transition and segments the story. Lifts a board out of slideshow (COMPOSED-CARDS §3).
examples: hook on blue, proof on paper, CTA back to blue

techniques.name: Metric-hero shot
techniques.description: The single strongest number, full-frame, its own beat, large and alone in the safe area — the capability-proof when a video has one hero number (CRAFT-BAR §A1/§A2).
examples: 30,000+ installs full-frame
110+ languages counting up

techniques.name: Count-up / reveal-in-steps
techniques.description: A number counting up, or a thing building, expressed as successive plates (A empty -> B half -> C full) the camera cuts/pushes between — NOT the end-state animated on one card (COMPOSED-CARDS §3).
examples: a dot-grid filling as a count rises
a line drawing on across three plates

techniques.name: Receipt / proof card
techniques.description: The artifact's actual output — a result, a list of sources, a diff, structured data — shown legibly as the capability-proof beat (CRAFT-BAR §A2).
examples: a structured-data receipt
a published-page confirmation

techniques.name: Two-symmetric-panels + one-word pivot
techniques.description: Before/after or them/you, two symmetric panels pivoting on a single word (COMPOSED-CARDS §4).
examples: 'without' / 'with' split on one word

techniques.name: Monospace NEW/COMING drumroll outro
techniques.description: A fixed two-line monospace card hard-cut on the beat, for a teaser close (COMPOSED-CARDS §4). Deferred-tease close, not a hard CTA.
examples: NEW <thing> / COMING <when>

techniques.name: Explicit CTA card
techniques.description: A labelled action (a 'Start free' pill, a concrete next step) held readable to the end — the REQUIRED close for a B-launch (CRAFT-BAR §B-launch). Never a bare URL or soft tagline.
examples: 'Start free at <domain>' pill

techniques.name: Motion-graphics overlay (title/lower-third/caption)
techniques.description: A programmatically animated title card, lower-third, animated captions, or overlay authored as an HTML/GSAP composition and rendered by the motion-graphics tool — designed motion between or over shots (glossary 'motion graphics').
examples: an animated lower-third naming a feature
kinetic captions tracking the VO

techniques.name: Ken Burns (move + zoom on a still)
techniques.description: A move-and-zoom over a still (a captured plate or a generated image) that fakes camera motion on a static picture, tied to a VO word (glossary).
examples: a slow push across a captured dashboard

techniques.name: Camera push-in / settle
techniques.description: A gentle push-in or a settle that lands the subject on the VO word — camera with intent, not an aimless drift (COMPOSED-CARDS §3).
examples: settle onto the hero number as it lands

techniques.name: Match-cut
techniques.description: A cut on a visual/graphic match between two plates so one shape becomes another (glossary transitions).
examples: a logo mark becoming a product icon

techniques.name: Real-UI capture (plate of the real product)
techniques.description: Screenshot a real site/app and animate a word-anchored camera over it — grounded, frame-exact product UI (capture-site skill). Needs a provided site/app.
examples: a real dashboard under a Ken-Burns tour

techniques.name: In-product one-action hook
techniques.description: A single plate of the product mid-action (the real question typed, the real thing triggered), cut just before the result — one plate, not a tour (COMPOSED-CARDS §4). The strongest opener per CRAFT-BAR §A4.
examples: the real query typed, cut before the answer

techniques.name: Edit caller-provided footage (b-roll / screen recording)
techniques.description: Trim/crop a caller-provided video asset (a screen recording, a take, stock) into a sub-clip, optionally with a Ken-Burns punch-in (edit-footage skill). Only when the brand supplied footage.
examples: a trimmed demo screen recording

techniques.name: Generative image asset
techniques.description: A generated still (background, illustration, icon, 3D-look asset) via the image provider — keyed (OpenAI/Gemini). Use as a plate under a camera move, not as the whole video.
examples: a generated glossy 3D icon as a hook plate

techniques.name: Generative video clip (cinematic b-roll)
techniques.description: A whole generated clip — cinematic kinetic motion graphics, a mood shot — not decomposed into plates. Needs a generative-video service key (not wired); surface as a roadmap reach per the lever.
examples: a cinematic abstract hook in the Katana style

techniques.name: Avatar presenter (talking head)
techniques.description: A talking-head presenter generated from the script by a hosted avatar provider — a human/UGC feel. Paid tier, hosted, not provisioned; surface per the lever.
examples: a presenter PiP over the product screen

techniques.name: Voiceover / narration
techniques.description: Synthesized word-timed narration (local Kokoro/Piper) — usually the spine the picture is timed to (voice-production skill).
examples: an even-cadence VO under the beats

techniques.name: Music bed
techniques.description: A background score under the video (local MusicGen / CC0 stock), ducked under the voice (build-soundtrack skill). A low bed is the floor for a production-quality piece (CRAFT-BAR §A5).
examples: an upbeat building electronic bed

techniques.name: SFX hits
techniques.description: Short, specific sounds tied to actions on the key beats — a reveal, the hero number, the CTA (click/tick/pop/hit/whoosh/swish). Scoped to the concept, never zero on a signature beat (CRAFT-BAR §A5).
examples: a rising-pitch tick run as pins multiply

techniques.name: Karaoke / word-timed captions
techniques.description: On-screen captions that highlight each word/phrase as it is spoken, anchored to the forced-alignment word timing (glossary). Good for silent/burned-in social cuts.
examples: burned-in kinetic captions for a muted social feed
